items.english: "I heard your voice, you know! Just after I'd come down the stone steps..."
(That is certainly mine! How is it I never noticed such a thing!)
notes: The referent, the telephone from p125, is left as 'that' as in the Japanese.

items.english: "There's no standing up to the missus. When she says come home, you come home, certain as anything!"
(I'll sell it, sell it, that's where I can get my breath back.) "Grandad, isn't there someone who would buy a telephone?"
notes: Interior flash and spoken appeal kept in one paragraph as in the Japanese, with the flash in parentheses.

items.english: "Can't a thing like that be sold straight off? By tomorrow, say?"
"I can't make out what this is about at all."

"Grandad, I've got the difficult work on me now, you see, that is... well, I can start it any time really, but as I am now I want to hold it in my head as long as I can, even if I go on holding it and holding it it doesn't matter, it's interesting! Mother and my wife wouldn't understand."
notes: Kept 'the difficult work' and 'hold it in my head' to the fixed concordance for p160. The Japanese slides from ore to boku mid speech; plain English I cannot show it.

items.english: "It's because I want to go on the trip. I'd like that too, so, well, let's go... but look, to do the work with my back to the wall like that, I hate it."
"Surely it is not as bad as that."
"Sell it for me, sell it for me! Sell the telephone for me..."
"...True enough, from now on there will be no need for a telephone here."
"Tomorrow! Tomorrow! Oh, I feel bright for no reason at all. Just being woken by it in the morning is more than I can bear."
notes: 'It' is the telephone and its morning call; left as in the Japanese.

items.english: "But that is because you asked the missus to do it, is it not?"
"Wouldn't it feel clean and good if it stopped coming every morning..."

data.say: Drunken telephone inspiration drafted with caretaker patter and parenthetical flashes kept rhythmically apart.
